Done. The Set-Cookie merge bug is fixed and verified.

## Root cause
In `src/context.ts` the `set res` setter iterated the existing response's headers and, for `set-cookie`, deleted the new response's own cookies and re-appended only the old ones:

```ts
const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
for (const cookie of cookies) { ... }   // new cookies lost
```

## Fix (`src/context.ts:414-435`)
Capture the incoming response's cookies once before the loop, then merge old + new:

```ts
const newCookies = _res.headers.getSetCookie()
...
if (k === 'set-cookie') {
  const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
  _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
  for (const cookie of [...cookies, ...newCookies]) { ... }
}
```

Capturing `newCookies` before the loop matters because `Headers.entries()` yields one `set-cookie` entry per old cookie; re-reading inside the loop would duplicate or clobber values. Non-cookie header behavior is unchanged.

## Tests (`src/context.test.ts`)
- Updated the existing re-assign test that asserted the buggy "old only" behavior to assert the merged `[...old, ...new]` result.
- Added regression test `'Should preserve both middleware and handler Set-Cookie headers when reassigning c.res'`, modeling a middleware-set cookie plus a handler `Response` with its own `Set-Cookie`.

## Verification
```
pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
```

The regression test was also confirmed to fail against the old semantics (`expected [ 'middleware=1; Path=/' ] to deeply equal [...]`). Changes touch only `src/context.ts` (+3/-1) and `src/context.test.ts` (+19/-3), are unstaged, and no git staging/commit was performed.
